episodes.196672: The interaction of Hurricane Kirk and another low pressure across the north Atlantic modulated the local weather pattern, pooling abundant moisture and promoting light winds in the region. Additionally, increasing instability due to the proximity of a mid to upper level trough favored deeper convection development each afternoon. This resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms each day along Puerto Rico, with daily amounts ranging from 2 to 4 inches, and localized higher amounts. With an elevated flooding risk, several flood and landslide reports were received.
episodes.197216: A large, mature waterspout was observed southeast of Duck Key in association with a thunderstorm embedded in deeply-moist, confluent lower tropospheric flow.
episodes.197323: A back-bent inverted trough and associated surface low pressure system resulted in increased moisture advection and rounds of showers and thunderstorms from the western Gulf of Mexico inland into Cameron, Willacy, and Kenedy County on October 4-5, 2024. This resulted in flooding in Los Fresnos, Texas on October 5, 2024.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Craig Key To West End Of Seven Mile Bridge Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A nearly-vertical, elephant trunk-like, mature waterspout was reported via social media south of the Toms Harbor Cut Bridge.  The condensation cloud extended all the way from the cloud base to the surface and a spray ring was present.  The movement was northwestward around 10 to 15 knots.
Bridge Puente Perfecto on road 103 impassable for small vehicles due to flood waters.
Flood waters from Rio Guadiana were affecting a bridge near Escuela Mercedes Rosado.

Emergency Management in Cameron County reported flooding in neighborhoods between Los Fresnos and Laureles due to runoff. There were reports of water depth of 3 feet in some areas. Two-day rainfall in the area ranged from 3.5 inches to nearly 6 inches.
